sections.h2: What does the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court record?
sections.html:
The Real Estate Division of the clerk's office records every Cobb County deed, plat, condominium floor plan, lien, UCC filing, general execution docket entry, military discharge, trade name and partnership filing. If you are selling a house in Cobb County, this is the office where the deed to your buyer gets filed and where the cancellation of your old security deed shows up after the loan is paid.

The division is at 10 East Park Square, Building C, in Marietta. The recording counter is on the 2nd floor, next to the State Court Building, and the deed room is on the 1st floor. The mailing address is P.O. Box 3430, Marietta, GA 30061. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., but the counters close at 4:30 p.m. for recording and copies. The main number is 770-528-2000.

Mail delivery between the Postal Service and the county mail room has changed, so the clerk asks filers to send documents well ahead of any deadline and to avoid e-filing late in the afternoon of a deadline day.

sections.h2: Who is allowed to file a deed on paper in Cobb County?
sections.html:
Since January 1, 2025, Georgia law under House Bill 1292 requires people filing for themselves to e-file real estate documents. Every person who e-files must first pass identity verification, including a photo check, through the Clerks' Authority portal at efile.gsccca.org. That portal is the only one through which real estate documents can be e-filed.

Paper filing is still open to these groups:

  • Georgia-licensed attorneys
  • Mortgage lenders, whether Georgia licensed or exempt
  • Mortgage servicers
  • Georgia-licensed surveyors
  • Georgia-licensed title insurance companies
  • Georgia-licensed real estate brokers or salespersons
  • Any public official

A member of one of those groups who chooses to e-file has to be verified like anyone else. In practice, an owner selling a Cobb County house through a closing attorney or title company never touches the filing, because the closing office submits the deed. An owner who prepares and files a deed without an attorney is the person most affected, and should finish the identity check before the recording date.

sections.h2: How much does the Cobb County clerk charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
The clerk's posted schedule, effective January 1, 2020, lists $25.00 for the first page of a deed and $0.00 for each added page. That covers warranty deeds, security deeds, assignments, satisfactions and cancellations. The office also has an online fee calculator for the exact total on a given filing. Offices accept cash, money order, cashier's check, certified check, and credit or debit cards, and a cardholder paying in person must appear with ID to sign the charge slip.

Extra cancellations, releases, satisfactions and assignments filed together are charged at the per-document amounts shown in the clerk's schedule. A single check can cover the recording fee and the taxes due, with the one exception of trade names. Make the check payable to Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court.

sections.h2: What is the Georgia transfer tax and how is it paid in Cobb County?
sections.html:
A warranty deed or quit claim deed filed in Cobb County needs a completed PT-61 form and payment of transfer tax at the time of recording, unless the transfer is exempt. The clerk cites O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 and 48-6-2. The PT-61 is completed online, printed and handed in with the deed, and the clerk keeps computers in the front lobby for people who need to fill it out on site.

The Georgia Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100, based on the sale price. The seller is liable for the tax, although the sales contract commonly shifts it to the buyer. Check your contract and settlement statement to see who is paying.

A separate intangible recording tax applies to a long-term note secured by real estate. The Department of Revenue prints it at $1.50 for each $500 or fractional part of the face amount. A security deed must be filed within 90 days of signing to avoid penalty and interest when the maturity date is more than three years out or the note is not exempt. That rule matters to your buyer's lender and rarely to you.

sections.h2: What does a Cobb County deed have to include?
sections.html:
The clerk lists the same basics for both warranty deeds and quit claim deeds. A deed has to carry the full legal description of the property, name the party transferring it, name the party receiving it, and be signed by the grantor with a witness and a notary. The clerk's office does not notarize, so bring the deed already notarized by a commissioned Georgia notary.

The two deed types protect a buyer differently. A warranty deed is the usual choice in a purchase and carries a guarantee that title is good and marketable, which is why buyers and lenders ask for it. A quit claim deed passes only whatever interest the signer holds, with no promise that title is clear or free of liens. It tends to show up in transfers between relatives or into a family entity.

  • Use the full legal description from your last deed, not the street address.
  • Have the notary and the witness sign in the same sitting as the grantor.
  • Complete the PT-61 before you arrive.
  • Bring one payment that covers recording fee and tax.

sections.h2: How do I get copies and check that my old mortgage was cancelled?
sections.html:
Copies of recorded documents can be printed from the clerk's website, made in the deed room on the 1st floor, or requested by mail with the clerk's request form and a self-addressed stamped envelope. Condo floor plans are handled the same way. Cancellations of security deeds are returned to the borrower unless the lender instructs otherwise, and in most cases the lender is the mortgage company. You can search the clerk's site to confirm a cancellation was filed. The office will not take payment on a lien, which has to be paid to the lien holder.

Building permits are a different office. The clerk's FAQ points owners to Cobb County or to the City of Marietta, depending on where the house sits, for fences, additions and similar work.

The clerk's real estate page also links to the Filing Activity Notification System at fans.gsccca.org.

sections.h2: What should a Cobb County seller know about the county itself?
sections.html:
Cobb County is a core county of the Atlanta area, formed in 1832 from Cherokee territory, with Marietta as the county seat and Mableton as the largest city. It covers about 345 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 766,149 residents, which made it the third most populous county in Georgia. Kennesaw Mountain, the highest point in the county, rises between Kennesaw and Marietta.

The Cobb County School District is the largest employer, with more than 15,000 employees, and the county is also home to the Home Depot support center, the Weather Channel, and the Lockheed Martin plant beside Dobbins Air Reserve Base. Interstates 75, 20, 285 and 575 cross the county. The tax commissioner's office bills the county and school district, and the cities of Acworth, Austell, Kennesaw, Mableton, Marietta, Smyrna and Powder Springs bill their own taxes.

Street addresses in the county all count from the southwest corner of the Marietta town square. If your house needs repairs or has a lien that has to be released before a deed can be recorded, talk to a closing attorney early, because the clerk cannot give legal advice.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Cobb County?
faqs.a: Record it with the Real Estate Division of the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court at 10 East Park Square, Building C, in Marietta. The office is open Monday to Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and recording counters close at 4:30 p.m. Call 770-528-2000 with questions.

faqs.q: Can I file my own deed on paper in Cobb County?
faqs.a: Usually not. Since January 1, 2025, people filing for themselves must e-file through efile.gsccca.org after verifying their identity with a photo check. Attorneys, lenders, servicers, surveyors, title companies, brokers and public officials may still file on paper.

faqs.q: How much is the Cobb County fee to record a deed?
faqs.a: The clerk's posted schedule lists $25.00 for the first page of a deed and $0.00 for added pages. Transfer tax is separate and is paid at recording with the PT-61. The clerk's online fee calculator gives an exact total, and one check can cover both fee and tax.

faqs.q: Who pays Georgia transfer tax when a Cobb County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller is liable for it under Georgia law, but the sales contract often assigns it to the buyer. The rate is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each added $100 of the price, as the Department of Revenue prints it. Your settlement statement shows who paid.

faqs.q: Does the Cobb County clerk notarize or give legal advice?
faqs.a: No on both counts. The clerk's office does not notarize, so bring a deed that is already signed before a notary with a witness. State law also bars the clerk's staff from giving legal advice, so a closing attorney should answer questions about what your deed should say.
